_comment: Configuration Management Plan generator. Phase 2B canonical template. Adding a new family is essentially copying this file, changing 'family' + 'title' + intro/approach prose, and authoring the family_questions groups appropriate to that domain. Groups carry a 'section' field that determines which document section they render under: system_overview (§3.x sub-section), approach (§4.x sub-section), continuous_monitoring (§6.x sub-section), or integration (§7).
title: Configuration Management Plan
description: Documents how the organization establishes, maintains, and monitors baseline configurations for the system. Covers the controls of the CM family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-128.
intro_template:
This Configuration Management Plan documents the configuration management approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, roles, and procedures used to manage the integrity of system components throughout the system's lifecycle.

The scope of this plan covers all hardware, software, firmware, and supporting documentation comprising the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-128 (Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information Systems) and the controls of the CM family in NIST SP 800-53 r5.
approach_template:
{system_name} uses {cm_tool} as the system of record for configuration items and baselines. Proposed changes are reviewed by a Configuration Control Board (CCB) chaired by {ccb_chair_role}, which meets on a {ccb_cadence} cadence. Baselines are documented and stored as follows: {baseline_storage}. The end-to-end change-request workflow is: {change_workflow}.

Additional details on the CCB, configuration audit strategy, exception management, backup approach, hardening sources, and documentation control are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Configuration baselines for {system_name} are reviewed against the active configuration on a defined cadence and any drift is reconciled through the change-management workflow described in section 4. The CCB is the authoritative body for evaluating drift findings, scheduling remediation, and approving exceptions. Findings, drift remediation actions, and CCB decisions are recorded in {cm_tool} and reviewed during periodic CM audits. Continuous monitoring of CM controls supports the broader ongoing-authorization strategy for the system. Detailed drift-detection automation, backup integration, and CM metrics are documented in the sub-sections below.
integration_template: This Configuration Management Plan does not stand alone. Control implementations described herein are referenced from the System Security Plan (SSP); deviations and findings flow into the Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M); vulnerability scan output and continuous-monitoring metrics inform CM activities. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where CM-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

prompts: Reference the CCB definition in §4.2 (chair, membership, cadence, quorum, decision thresholds).
Describe approval thresholds — what changes need majority vs unanimous; what changes require AO concurrence.
Document separation of duties: who can submit changes vs review vs approve vs implement vs verify.
Identify the enforcement mechanism (RBAC / Git branch protection / SCCM permission groups / GPO).
Address the emergency change pathway — criteria, who can authorize, retroactive review window.
State the security-impact analysis (CM-4) requirement and its position in the workflow.
evidence_suggestions: Sample emergency change record + retroactive review

extra_fields.label: Approval thresholds
extra_fields.help: Map change types to required approval levels (routine / standard / emergency / security-impacting).

extra_fields.label: Separation of duties
extra_fields.help: Who submits / reviews / approves / implements / verifies. The same person should not own consecutive steps where it allows unilateral change.

extra_fields.label: Enforcement mechanism
extra_fields.help: Technical control that enforces the workflow (e.g., 'Git branch protection requires 2 reviewers including a security team member; main branch deploys via Ansible only from CCB-approved tags').

prompts: List the privileged role/group in your IAM that holds change-modification rights.
Describe how membership is reviewed and approved (cadence, approving role).
Cross-reference AC-6 (Least Privilege) — CM-5 access restrictions are enforced through the AC-6 implementation.
State the enforcement mechanism (RBAC in SCCM / OS-level privileges / Git CODEOWNERS / cloud IAM policy).
Identify any logging that captures privileged change events for AU-2 / AU-12 visibility.
evidence_suggestions: IAM group / role membership report (privileged CM group)
Audit log sample showing privileged change events
Onboarding / offboarding procedure for the privileged group

extra_fields.label: Who can SUBMIT changes
extra_fields.help: Roles that can open a change request.

extra_fields.label: Who can APPROVE changes
extra_fields.help: Roles that hold approval authority (typically the CCB or its designees).

extra_fields.label: Who can IMPLEMENT changes
extra_fields.help: Roles with technical permission to deploy approved changes.

extra_fields.label: AC-6 cross-reference
extra_fields.help: How this ties to your AC-6 (Least Privilege) implementation.

extra_fields.label: Enforcement mechanism (RBAC etc.)
extra_fields.help: Technical enforcement (e.g., 'AWS IAM permission boundary on the CMOps role; SCCM compliance baseline restricts deployment console access').

prompts: Cite each authoritative configuration source (DISA STIGs, CIS Benchmarks, vendor hardening guides) — see §4.3 for the catalog.
Describe how baselines are derived from those sources (manual mapping vs automated import).
Document the deviation register: where exceptions to the baseline live, who approves them, and how they're tracked.
State the enforcement mechanism (Ansible playbook, SCCM compliance baseline, GPO, Salt state, etc.).
Specify the verification cadence (how often actual config is compared to documented baseline).
evidence_suggestions: Ansible playbook / Salt states repository link
Sample baseline document for one CI type (workstation / server / appliance)

extra_fields.label: Hardening sources cited (specific to this control)
extra_fields.help: Reference the specific STIGs / Benchmarks applicable to this system. Suggestions are common picks; customize.

extra_fields.label: Deviation register location
extra_fields.help: Where approved deviations / exceptions to baseline are tracked (URL, document path, ticketing query).

extra_fields.label: Enforcement mechanism
extra_fields.help: How baseline settings are actively enforced on the system (push-config tool, immutable infrastructure, etc.).

prompts: Enumerate the set of allowed services / ports / protocols (or reference a baseline document that does).
Identify services that are explicitly disabled in the baseline.
Describe the application allowlisting approach (AppLocker / WDAC / OS-level allowlist / endpoint management product).
Address how the system limits inbound and outbound network exposure (security groups, host firewall, network segmentation).
Mention how unnecessary functions are reviewed periodically (CM-7(1)).

extra_fields.label: Allowed services / ports / protocols
extra_fields.help: Enumerate or reference the authorized set. Include both inbound and outbound where relevant.

extra_fields.label: Explicitly disabled services
extra_fields.help: Services / features turned off that the OS or application would enable by default (e.g., Telnet, FTP, RDP for non-admin VLANs).

extra_fields.label: Application allowlisting approach
extra_fields.help: How application execution is controlled. Reference the CM-7(5) enhancement if applicable.

prompts: Identify the system of record for inventory (CMDB, AWS Config, ServiceNow, Excel, etc.).
Enumerate the ATTRIBUTES tracked per CI — see the structured field below.
Describe how inventory is updated (event-driven vs scheduled, automated vs manual).
State the reconciliation cadence (how often actual systems are compared to inventory).
Address ownership: who is responsible for inventory accuracy, and what review cadence applies.

extra_fields.label: Inventory tooling (system of record)
extra_fields.help: Primary system that holds inventory (e.g., 'ServiceNow CMDB synced nightly with AWS Config and Active Directory').

extra_fields.label: Reconciliation cadence
extra_fields.help: How often inventory is reconciled with active state (e.g., 'continuous via AWS Config rules; monthly manual spot-check').

prompts: Identify the license-tracking system that tracks software usage rights for the system.
Describe how license counts are verified against actual deployed instances.
If software provenance is tracked (vendor source, signed installers, SBOM), describe the approach — supports SR / SA-12 alignment.
Address how unauthorized software acquisition is prevented (procurement gating, package allowlist).
evidence_suggestions: Software bill of materials (SBOM) for primary components

extra_fields.label: License tracking system
extra_fields.help: System that holds license records (e.g., 'Flexera ITAM', 'Snow License Manager', 'spreadsheet').

extra_fields.label: Software provenance approach
extra_fields.help: How software origin is verified. SBOM availability, signed-package verification, vendor authenticity checks.

prompts: Describe the enforcement mechanism preventing user-installed software (endpoint management, OS-level UAC / SUDO restrictions, AppLocker / WDAC).
Document the exception process for legitimate user-installed needs (developers, kiosks, etc.).
Address detection: how unauthorized installs are discovered after the fact (HIDS / EDR / scheduled scans).
State the user-acceptable-use policy that articulates the restriction to end users.
evidence_suggestions: EDR / HIDS detection rule for unauthorized installations

extra_fields.label: Restriction enforcement mechanism
extra_fields.help: Tooling and OS-level controls that block user-installed software.

extra_fields.label: Exception process
extra_fields.help: How a legitimate exception is requested, approved, and tracked. Reference the exception management group in §4.5.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Tools, baselines, and the change-request flow that everything else hangs off.

questions.label: Configuration management tool / repository of record
questions.help: Tool, repo, or system holding your authoritative configuration baselines (e.g., GitHub Enterprise, Ansible Automation Platform, SCCM, Puppet Enterprise, Chef, Salt).

questions.label: How are baselines documented and stored?
questions.help: Where baseline configurations live and how they're versioned. Example: 'In a Git repository under config/baselines/, tagged at each release. Hardware inventory tracked in ServiceNow CMDB.'

questions.label: Change-request workflow
questions.help: Workflow from change request through review, approval, implementation, and verification. Mention tooling (Jira, ServiceNow), approval thresholds, and the emergency change pathway.

family_questions.label: Configuration Control Board
family_questions.description: Membership, quorum, decision authority, and emergency-change criteria.

questions.label: CCB chair role
questions.help: Role title (e.g., 'Director of Engineering') rather than a named individual; the role outlasts the person.

questions.label: CCB voting membership
questions.help: Roles that hold votes. Example list: System Owner, ISSO, ISSM, Engineering Lead, Network Lead.

questions.label: Quorum requirement
questions.help: Number or percentage of voting members required to make a binding decision (e.g., '4 of 6', 'simple majority').

questions.label: Decision thresholds
questions.help: What changes require simple majority vs unanimous? What's the threshold for changes affecting the security posture?

questions.label: Emergency change criteria + pathway
questions.help: What qualifies as an emergency change? Who can authorize? What's the retroactive review window?

questions.label: Documentation standards
questions.help: What's recorded for each CCB meeting? Where are minutes stored? Retention?

family_questions.label: Configuration Item Identification
family_questions.description: How CIs are named, classified, and related to each other.

questions.label: CI naming convention
questions.help: How CIs are named, e.g., '<env>-<role>-<serial>' or 'aws/<account>/<region>/<resource_id>'.

questions.label: Relationship-mapping approach
questions.help: How dependencies between CIs are documented (e.g., 'CMDB relationship table with hosts → applications → databases'). Critical for impact analysis.

questions.label: Version-control structure
questions.help: Branch / tag / release strategy used to track CI versions.

family_questions.label: Hardening sources
family_questions.description: Authoritative configuration sources cited for CM-6 baseline composition.

questions.label: Cited hardening sources
questions.help: Add each authoritative source. Suggestions auto-populate one click; you can edit or add custom entries.

family_questions.label: Configuration Audit Strategy
family_questions.description: Functional vs physical audits, frequency, roles, and reconciliation.

questions.label: Audit frequency
questions.help: How often each audit type runs (e.g., 'FCA quarterly, PCA annually').

questions.label: Independent assessor role
questions.help: Role responsible for independent verification (e.g., 'Internal Audit', 'Third-party assessor').

questions.label: System-owner role in audit
questions.help: What the System Owner provides / signs off during the audit.

questions.label: Reconciliation process
questions.help: How discrepancies between audited configuration and the documented baseline are reconciled, who decides, and how it's tracked.

family_questions.label: Exception Management
family_questions.description: Approval workflow, time-bound waivers, POA&M linkage, and revalidation.

questions.label: Deviation / waiver approval workflow
questions.help: Who can request, who reviews, who approves a deviation from baseline. Reference CCB if relevant.

questions.label: Maximum waiver duration
questions.help: Hard limit on how long a waiver can stand before it must be revisited (e.g., '90 days', '6 months').

questions.label: POA&M linkage
questions.help: How active waivers are tracked in the POA&M (e.g., 'Each waiver opens a POA&M item with milestone = waiver expiration').

questions.label: Revalidation cadence
questions.help: How often open waivers are reviewed for continued applicability.

family_questions.label: Backup & Recoverability of Baselines
family_questions.description: Recoverability, versioning, and integrity protection for configuration data (CM-9 / CP overlap).

questions.label: Recoverability approach
questions.help: How baselines + supporting configuration data can be restored if lost or corrupted. RTO / RPO if defined.

questions.label: Versioning scheme
questions.help: How successive baseline versions are tracked (Git tags, retention policy on snapshots, etc.).

questions.label: Integrity protection
questions.help: How baselines are protected from undetected modification (signed Git tags, SHA-256 hashes in CMDB, etc.).

family_questions.label: Drift Detection Automation
family_questions.description: Tooling, frequency, alerting, and integration with SIEM / ticketing.

questions.label: Drift detection tooling
questions.help: What runs the periodic comparison (SCCM compliance baselines, Tenable, Ansible idempotent run, custom scripts, etc.).

questions.label: Scan frequency
questions.help: How often drift detection runs (e.g., 'continuous', 'daily', 'weekly').

questions.label: Alert thresholds
questions.help: What level of drift triggers a page vs a daily summary. How false positives are tuned out.

questions.label: SIEM / ticketing integration
questions.help: Where drift findings flow (SIEM rule, Jira queue, ServiceNow incident). Owner of triage.

family_questions.label: CM Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate CM control effectiveness over time.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: % changes routed through CCB (vs emergency / out-of-band)
questions.help: Add each metric your program reports on. Suggestions are common picks; customize as needed.

family_questions.label: Configuration Documentation Control
family_questions.description: Versioning schema, approval signatures, and retention requirements.

questions.label: Versioning schema
questions.help: Format used for plan / baseline document versions (e.g., 'MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH', '<year>.<release>').

questions.label: Retention period
questions.help: How long approved baseline documents and supporting records are retained (e.g., '7 years post-decommission', 'per NARA GRS 4.2').

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the CM control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.5').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for CM findings
questions.help: Convention used to identify CM-related POA&M items (e.g., 'CM-' or 'POAM-CM-####').

questions.label: RA-5 scan source feeding CM
questions.help: Vulnerability scanner whose output drives CM remediation (e.g., 'Tenable.sc Container A', 'Nessus Manager').

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document that ties CM continuous-monitoring activities to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation; excludes separately authorized systems to which the system is connected.
A documented, formally reviewed and agreed-upon set of specifications for a system at a given point in time. Serves as the reference against which subsequent changes are evaluated.
A formal proposal to modify a configuration item, submitted for review and approval through the configuration-management workflow.
Entity responsible for the implementation, assessment, and monitoring of a common control inherited by one or more information systems.
An independent verification that a configuration item conforms to its specified configuration. Includes both functional and physical configuration audits.
The systematic evaluation, approval/disapproval, and implementation of changes to configuration items, performed after formal establishment of their baselines.
An organizational body responsible for evaluating proposed changes to configuration baselines and approving or disapproving their implementation.
The process of selecting items for configuration management, naming them, and identifying the relationships between them.
An aggregation of hardware, software, firmware, or any combination thereof, that is designated for configuration management.
A repository for storing configuration items and the relationships between them; supports configuration status accounting.
The recording and reporting of information needed to manage configuration items effectively, including the status of proposed changes and the implementation status of approved changes.
Unintended divergence between an active configuration and its documented baseline. Detected through periodic comparison and reconciled via the change-management workflow.
Verification that a configuration item's functional and performance characteristics meet its specifications.
Initial approved technical documentation describing the functional, interoperability, and interface characteristics of a configuration item.
Control whose implementation is shared between a common control provider and the information system itself.
A parameter in a NIST 800-53 control that the implementing organization must specify (e.g., a frequency, threshold, role, or selection from a set of options) to make the control assessable.
Verification that the physical embodiment of a configuration item matches its as-built documentation.
Approved configuration documentation describing the configuration of a configuration item as it is to be produced or fielded.
Analysis conducted by qualified personnel to determine the extent to which proposed changes could affect the security posture of a system.
An ODV form in NIST 800-53 where the organization must choose one (or one-or-more) options from a defined list.
Process by which an organization adjusts a control baseline by selecting, removing, or modifying controls and enhancements to align with system-specific risk.
A formally approved, time-bound deviation from a baseline configuration or control requirement.
